blogs.title: Why Token‑Level Pitfalls Hurt Big‑Llama: The GSPO Solution Explained
blogs.description: Dive into the core problem that has been crippling state‑of‑the‑art RL for large language models—token‑level importance ratios and how they corrupt gradients. This post walks readers through the instability in GRPO, why high‑variance off‑policy corrections at each token cause catastrophic model collapse, and how Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO) redefines the importance ratio at the entire sequence level to bring stability back to RL training.

blogs.title: From Tokens to Sequences: How GSPO Makes Reward Alignment Natural
blogs.description: Rewards in RL for language models kick in only after a full response is produced. This article explains why aligning the reward with the same granularity used for discounting and clipping (i.e., an entire sequence) leads to cleaner gradients. It breaks down GSPO’s sequence‑level clipping, length normalization, and advantage estimation, showing readers how a single objective can scale effortlessly to longer generations and larger models.

blogs.title: MoE Meets RL: How GSPO Eliminates Expert Activation Volatility
blogs.description: Mixture‑of‑Experts models add sparsity but also introduce volatile expert activations that wreck token‑level importance ratios. This post recounts the legacy Routing Replay trick, its runtime overhead, and demonstrates how GSPO’s sequence likelihood ignores per‑token expert changes, thereby stabilizing MoE RL training without architectural gymnastics.

blogs.title: GSPO vs GRPO: A Mathematical Peek Behind Stable Training
blogs.description: This post takes a deeper dive into the gradient derivations of GSPO and GRPO, highlighting how token weighting in GRPO accumulates noise while GSPO weights tokens uniformly through the sequence importance ratio. Readers will learn why GSPO drastically reduces stochasticity in policy updates and how this translates into better sample efficiency.

blogs.title: Practical Guide: Implementing GSPO on Your Existing RL Pipeline
blogs.description: For engineers ready to experiment with GSPO, this blog walks through the key code‑level changes: computing sequence ratios by exponentiating per‑token log probabilities, averaging advantages over groups, and setting proper clipping ranges. It also covers handling precision differences between training and inference engines—an often overlooked pitfall when moving from standard PPO to GSPO.
